newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent pushes higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent pushes higher on short covering.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures pushed higher early on Tuesday as players bought to cover their short positions, while gas oil also opened a slightly firmer.
August Brent was 31 cents higher at $18.17 a barrel by 1000 GMT. July gas oil futures were up $1.25 at $163.00 a tonne.
Brokers said Brent prices were likely to remain rangebound.
"I don't think it's got the legs to go higher," one broker said. "We are looking for a lid on the market at around $18.15."
But brokers said the market was well supported and unlikely to revisit the fresh 13-month lows set last week.
"The difference this week is that when there is a dip the bid is always there," one said.
At current levels the market was seen bottoming out.
"We're really approaching levels where people are not prepared to sell," one said. But he added: "We're not bullish yet, we need a few more days of consolidation."
Dealers said one wave of buying was tending to kick in around $18.00 and below that another at $17.85.

Gas oil, meanwhile, was also trading in a tight range but in thin volume. Dealers cited $161.50 as a buying level for those players who short of paper and they said there was a lid on the market at around $164.50.
